claims.text: The GI journal advertised Konark Stone Carving as accepted for stone statues and statuettes of gods and goddesses, nature and human forms, candle stands, Konark wheels, flower vases, mobile holders and key rings.

quotes.quote: Goods : Statues and statuettes of gods and goddesses, nature and human forms, Candle stand, Konark wheel , Flower vase, Mobile holder, Key rings made of stone.
made of stone falling in Class 19 is hereby advertised as accepted

claims.text: The GI journal names Konark in Puri district with its nearby areas, and Bhubaneswar with its outskirts, as the main areas producing Konark stone carving.

quotes.locator: G.I. Application Number 87, (H) Geographical area of production, p. 59
quotes.quote: The main geographical areas of production of konark stone carving are Konark (district Puri, Orissa, India) and near-by areas and Bhubaneswar (Orissa, India) and its outskirts.

claims.text: The GI journal describes the craft as reducing a block of stone to a finished state with a variety of tools.

quotes.locator: G.I. Application Number 87, (J) Method of production, p. 61
quotes.quote: The process is carried by the reduction of a block of stone to a finished state using a variety of tools.

claims.text: Stone carving is a very major handicraft of Odisha, whose artisans carve exact replicas of the original temple sculptures besides a variety of other items.

quotes.quote: Stone carving is a very major handicraft of Odisha.
their deft hands can and do chisel and carve exact replicas of the original temple sculptures besides producing a variety of other items.

claims.text: The GI application names its raw material, serpentine stone, which it says other craftsmen do not employ, as the most important feature of Konark stone carving.

quotes.quote: The most important feature of Konark stone carving is the raw material. Konark stone carving utilizes serpentine stone, which is not employed by other craftsman.

claims.text: The GI journal says present-day stone carving products range from sculptures, vases and interior decorations to large monuments.

quotes.locator: G.I. Application Number 87, (G) Description of goods, p. 59
quotes.quote: The present day stone carving products range from sculptures, vases, interior decorations to large monuments.

claims.text: The Orissa Reference Annual counts stone carving among the state's crafts of artistic excellence and says most of its handicrafts have their roots in the rituals of Lord Jagannath of Puri.

quotes.quote: Significantly, most handicrafts in the state have their roots in the rituals and traditions of the famed Lord Jagannath of Puri.
Brass work, silver filigree work, stone carving, applique work and pattachitra are all illustrations of artistic excellence.

claims.text: The GI journal says the craftspersons of the Kalinga School built masterpieces such as the Sun Temple at Konark.

quotes.locator: G.I. Application Number 87, (I) Proof of origin, p. 59
quotes.quote: The crafts persons of the Kalinga School have built masterpieces like the Sun Temple, Konark

claims.text: The GI application says the work is confined to the Pathuria caste, with surnames such as Das, Mistri, Nayak and Maharana, as an Odia inscription of 1604 mentions.

quotes.locator: G.I. Application Number 87, proof of origin, p. 61
quotes.quote: The work is confined to people of Pathurias caste with surnames of Das, Mistri, Nayak, Maharana, etc. this has been mentioned in the year 1604 in an oriya inscription

claims.text: The GI application dates the art of Konark stone carving back to the late 6th or early 7th century AD.

quotes.locator: G.I. Application Number 87, proof of origin, p. 61
quotes.quote: The art dates back to the late 6th century or early 7th century AD

claims.text: The Orissa Reference Annual 2005 says stone carving art is perhaps the most ancient, as the 2200 years old elephant sculpture of Dhauli shows.

quotes.quote: ORISSA REFERENCE ANNUAL - 2005
Stone carving art is perhaps the most ancient, as is evident from the 2200 years old elephant sculpture of Dhauli.

claims.text: The Sun Temple at Konark was built in the 13th century under King Narasimha Deva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty, who reigned from 1238 to 1264.

quotes.quote: Built in the 13th century, it is one of India's most famous Brahman sanctuaries.
The Sun Temple is an exceptional testimony, in physical form, to the 13th-century Hindu Kingdom of Orissa, under the reign of Narasimha Deva I (AD 1238-1264).
It was built c. 1250 CE by King Narasimhadeva I (r. 1238-1264 CE) of the Eastern Ganga dynasty (8th century CE - 15th century CE).

claims.text: UNESCO describes the Sun Temple at Konark as the culmination of Kalingan temple architecture, with all its defining elements in complete and perfect form.

quotes.quote: The Sun Temple is the culmination of Kalingan temple architecture, with all its defining elements in complete and perfect form.

claims.text: In a legend UNESCO records, building the Konark temple mobilised 1,200 workers for 12 years under the architect Bisu Moharana.

quotes.quote: the temple has raised up those lovely legends which are affiliated everywhere with absolute works of art
its construction caused the mobilization of 1,200 workers for 12 years. The architect, Bisu Moharana, having left his birthplace to devote himself to his work

claims.text: Sculptor Pravakara Maharana credits his success to the 1,200 artisans who, he says, worked for 12 years to build the Sun Temple, and calls himself one of their descendants.

quotes.quote: gave credit for his success to the 1,200 artisans who had constructed the world famous Sun Temple at Konark in 13th century
Those artisans had worked rigorously for 12 years to construct the magnificent structure.
I consider myself as one of their descendants

claims.text: Odisha Tourism says the progeny of the artisans who built temples such as Lingaraj, Mukteswar and the Sun God's temple chariot at Konark have kept their forefathers' sculptural traditions alive.

quotes.quote: The progeny of these artisans who built the magnificent temples of Parsurameswar, Mukteswar, Lingaraj, Puri and that wonder in stone, the temple chariot of the Sun God at Konark
have kept alive the sculptural traditions of their forefathers

claims.text: Odisha's stone-carving traditions are carried on from generation to generation, and a few ancient texts on the art that have survived are followed closely.

quotes.quote: The traditions are carried on from generation to generation and a few ancient texts on the art which have survived are followed closely.

claims.text: Paramparik Karigar writes that sculptors of India's stone carving traditions follow the principles of the Shilpa Shastras, a doctrine containing guidelines on stone measurements and techniques of sculpting.

quotes.quote: Some of the finest examples of stone carving in India have evolved around religion
The sculptors follow the principles of the Shilpa Shastras , a doctrine containing guidelines on stone measurements and techniques of sculpting.

claims.text: A Millennium Post feature says the artists work with the traditional chisel and hammer and faithfully follow age-old doctrines laid down in texts written by the legendary Vishwakarma.

quotes.quote: The artists of today continue to work with the traditional tools of chisel and hammer, and faithfully follow the age-old doctrines laid down in the texts written by the legendary Vishwakarma to recreate these masterpieces.

claims.text: The GI application calls Konark one of the most ancient places of stone carving and a centre of its origin, saying its artisans originate from Konark and nearby villages.

quotes.locator: Form GI-1, name of the geographical indication
quotes.quote: Konark is one of the most ancient places where stone carving has been practiced. This is one ofthe centers of origin of the art.

quotes.locator: Form GI-1, name of the geographical indication
quotes.quote: Although this art has been practiced in other places around Konark like Bhubaneswar, the artisians and craftmen orginate from konark and a nearby cluster of villages.

claims.text: UNESCO's short description presents the Konark temple as the sun god Surya's chariot, its 24 wheels decorated with symbolic designs and led by a team of six horses.

quotes.quote: the temple at Konarak is a monumental representation of the sun god Surya's chariot; its 24 wheels are decorated with symbolic designs and it is led by a team of six horses.

claims.text: The temple represents the Sun God's chariot with twelve pairs of wheels drawn by seven horses, and its 24 carved wheels are each about 3 m in diameter.

quotes.quote: the temple represents a chariot of the Sun God, with twelve pairs of wheels drawn by seven horses evoking its movement across the heavens
On the north and south sides are 24 carved wheels, each about 3 m in diameter
in the form of a colossal chariot with twelve pairs of lavishly-ornamented wheels, drawn by seven richly-caparisoned, galloping horses

claims.text: Early Europeans sailing the Bay of Bengal called the Konark temple the 'Black Pagoda' and the Jagannatha temple the 'White Pagoda', after its white plaster.

quotes.quote: The early Europeans traversing this sea referred to the Jagannatha temple as the 'White Pagoda' owing to its white plaster (now removed after restoration) and Konarak as the 'Black Pagoda'.
it served as a landmark for sailors sailing the Bay of Bengal

claims.text: The name Konark combines two Sanskrit words, kona, meaning corner or angle, and arka, meaning the sun.

quotes.quote: The word 'Konark' is a combination of two Sanskrit words kona (corner or angle) and arka (the sun).

claims.text: On the Konark Sun Temple, the sculptured designs were carved after the stones had been set into place.

quotes.quote: The designs were carved after the stones had been set into place.

claims.text: Temple panels at Konark that represent King Narasimhadeva in various roles are made from pink and green khondalite.

quotes.quote: Panels represent King Narasimhadeva in various roles
These are made from pink and green khondalite

claims.text: The V&A's relief of King Narasimha I with his spiritual advisor, made in the 2nd quarter of the 13th century, belongs to a series that originally decorated the Konark Sun Temple's walls.

quotes.quote: King Narasimha and his spiritual advisor
2nd quarter of 13th century (made)
This relief is one of a series depicting aspects of royal Vaishnava worship in Odisha and is associated with the Sun Temple at Konarak.
this series originally decorated the temple's walls

claims.text: Sculptor Sudarshan Sahoo was born in Puri in 1939 and has worked with the medium of stone and wood.

quotes.locator: Know more about the master sculptor
quotes.quote: The sculptor, who has nearly 70 years of experience, was born in Odisha's Puri in 1939.
Sudarshan Sahoo was born in 1939 and has been working with the medium of stone and wood

claims.text: Sudarshan Sahoo received the National Award in 1981, the Padma Shri in 1988 and the Shilp Guru Award in 2003.

quotes.quote: He was bestowed with the National Award in 1981; the Padma Shri in 1988; the Shilp Guru Award in 2003
Sudarshan is also a recipient of the National Award for Stone Carving (1981). Seven years later, in 1988, he was awarded the Padma Shri and, in 2003, the Shilp Guru Award.

claims.text: Sudarshan Sahoo was selected for the Padma Vibhushan award 2021 and was conferred with it by President Ram Nath Kovind.

quotes.quote: Noted sculptor Sudarshan Sahoo has been selected for Padma Vibhushan award 2021, for his exceptional and distinguished service in the field of art.
was conferred with the Padma Vibhushan, the second highest civilian award of the country by President Ram Nath Kovind

claims.text: Sudarshan Sahoo established the Sudarshan Crafts Museum in Puri in 1977 as a training-cum-production centre.

quotes.quote: He established the Sudarshan Crafts Museum in 1977, a training-cumproduction centre in Puri.

quotes.locator: Know more about the master sculptor
quotes.quote: In 1977, he set up Sudarshan Crafts Museum in Puri for artists to display their work in a streamlined space.

claims.text: In 1991 Sudarshan Sahoo set up the Sudarshan Art and Crafts Village in Bhubaneswar, a gurukul following the guru-shishya parampara to train other artists.

quotes.quote: In 1991, he set up the Sudarshan Art and Crafts Village in Bhubaneswar, which follows the ancient guru-shishya parampara

quotes.locator: Know more about the master sculptor
quotes.quote: He also established a Gurukul in 1991, the Sudarshan Art and Crafts village, in Bhubaneswar, to train other artists.

claims.text: The Sudarshan Crafts Museum, a project supported by the Government of Odisha, and the Sudarshan Arts and Crafts Village aim to preserve Odisha's traditional sculpting craft and train future craftsmen in wood, stone and fibreglass, with free boarding.

quotes.locator: Know more about the master sculptor
quotes.quote: The Sudarshan Crafts Museum, a project supported by the Government of Odisha, along with Sudarshan Arts and Crafts Village aim at preserving the traditional craft of sculpting in Odisha and training future craftsmen in creating sculptures with wood, stone and fiberglass.

quotes.locator: Know more about the master sculptor
quotes.quote: The institution provides its craftsmen with all the facilities, including a free of cost boarding facility.

claims.text: Sudarshan Sahoo carved the Jataka Tales at the Dhauli Peace Pagoda in 1971, and his stone panel on the life of Buddha was installed at Milton Keynes in 1980.

quotes.locator: Know more about the master sculptor
quotes.quote: He created beautiful carvings of the Jataka Tales at the Dhauli Peace Pagoda in 1971 which earned him worldwide recognition and appreciation.

quotes.locator: Know more about the master sculptor
quotes.quote: a stone panel based around the life of Buddha was installed in Milton Keynes, London, in 1980.

claims.text: Paramparik Karigar writes that, on the invitation of the Buddha Sangha, London, Sudarshan Sahoo carved the Jataka Tales in the Buddhist Pagoda at Milton Keynes.

quotes.quote: Sudarshan Sahoo was born in 1939 and has been working with the medium of stone and wood
On the invitation of the Buddha Sangha, London, he carved the Jataka Tales in the Buddhist Pagoda at Milton Keynes.

claims.text: Padma Shri sculptor Pravakara Maharana, whose father carved wooden figures, began training at the Orissa State Handicraft Training Centre in Bhubaneswar in 1975 and has carved stone since.

quotes.quote: Noted sculptor Pravakara Maharana, who has been felicitated with Padma Shri award
his father Sadhucharan was a carpenter and had expertise in carving wooden figures
my father enrolled me to the Orissa State Handicraft Training Centre in Bhubaneswar in 1975. Since then, I have been carving stones

claims.text: Pravakara Maharana trained under eminent artisans including Bhubaneswar Mahapatra and Satyabadi Maharana, and has received a state handicraft award and the Shilpiguru award.

quotes.quote: who received training from eminent artisans like Bhubaneswar Mahapatra and Satyabadi Maharana, considers his father as his first teacher
Earlier, I received state handicraft award and Shilpiguru award.

claims.text: Sculptor Pravakara Maharana is a resident of Sujanagar near Gop, which the Puri district administration lists among the blocks of Puri district.

quotes.quote: said the noted sculptor, a resident of Sujanagar near Gop

claims.text: In December 2016 the EPCH ran a 25-day design and technical development workshop in stone craft at Bhubaneswar for 40 selected artisans under master craftsperson and National Awardee Susil Kumar Maharana.

quotes.quote: A Design & Technological Development workshop in stone craft for General artisans at Bhubaneswar sanctioned
with 40 artisans under the guidance of master crafts person Susil Kumar Maharana The workshop is to commence from 5th Dec for a period of 25 days.
Inauguration 5th Dec, 2016 meeting
Master crafts person Mr., Susil Kumar Maharana (National Awardee).
40 candidates were selected on the basis of their skill
The schedule of workshop was 5 hours daily from 11.00 a.m. - 4.00 p.m. for 25 days.

claims.text: During meetings in Bhubaneswar in October 2016, the EPCH designer was told that most of the skill at Bhubaneswar is average while a few households are very skilled.

quotes.quote: After contacting the DCH office at Bhubaneswar, I visited their office on the of 26th October, 2016
He informed that most of the skill at Bhubaneswar is average while a few households are very skilled.

claims.text: During the same 2016 meetings in Bhubaneswar, the EPCH designer was told that women mostly take up the craft as a vocation, are not specifically from artisan families and supply local retailers.

quotes.quote: After contacting the DCH office at Bhubaneswar, I visited their office on the of 26th October, 2016
We had a good discussion about the craft, need for diversification
Women mostly do it as a vocation and are not specifically from the artisan families and supply to local retailers.

claims.text: An official of the Development Commissioner (Handicrafts) told the EPCH designer in 2016 that exports dealt with the same product line and were steadily declining.

quotes.quote: I visited their office on the of 26th October, 2016 and met with Mrs. Shalija
Mr. A.K Panigrahy, the Asst. Director, DC (H)
Mr. Panigrahy has been extremely helpful, supportive and has displayed keenness in the development of the products.
Exports, he says, deals with the same product line and is steadily on the decline.

claims.text: The EPCH report says the Bhubaneswar carvers market their products from home, at national and state fairs through Utkalika, at Ekamra Haat in Bhubaneswar, through Sasha in Kolkata and by custom orders.

quotes.quote: The products marking ting has been done through themselves at home, marketing in national fair and state fair through utkalika, Ekamra hat-Bhubaneswar, sasha Kolkata, customized order by individuals etc.

claims.text: The EPCH report says the major product is mythological story bases in frames of different sizes, while diversification has reached candle stands, planters and decorative wall planters.

quotes.quote: Major product is mythological story base in frame of different sizes hold the share.
Diversification has been done on many products but only product like candle stand, planter, decorative wall planter etc.

claims.text: In the GI method of production, the basic design is traced on the stone and given a crude shape, then the final carving is carried out and the items are polished.

quotes.locator: G.I. Application Number 87, (J) Method of production, p. 61
quotes.quote: The process of doing is the basic design is traced on the stone and it is given a crude shape. The final carving is then carried out and the items are polished.

claims.text: In the GI journal's process, the block of stone is broken down into main planes or areas, following the form of the desired shape.

quotes.locator: G.I. Application Number 87, (J) Method of production, Process, p. 61
quotes.quote: The block of stone is broken down in to main planes or areas, following form of the desired shape.

claims.text: In the GI journal's process, the surface is drilled to various desired depths and unwanted material is removed.

quotes.locator: G.I. Application Number 87, (J) Method of production, Process, p. 61
quotes.quote: Surface is drilled to various desired depths and unwanted material removed.

claims.text: After the rough body outline, the intricate work is made, and tool marks are then removed with flat chisels.

quotes.locator: G.I. Application Number 87, (J) Method of production, Process, p. 61
quotes.quote: rough body outline is made. Intricate work is then made. Tool marks are removed with flat chisels.

claims.text: Odisha Tourism says that whether the stone is hard or soft, an outline is first drawn on stone already cut to size, and once it is incised the figure is brought out by removing unwanted portions.

quotes.quote: Whether the stone is hard or soft a sort of outline is first drawn on the stone which is already cut to the appropriate size. Once the outline is incised indicating the shape, the final figure is brought out by removing the unwanted portions.

claims.text: Odisha Tourism says harder stones are worked by chiselling out the extra material, while softer stones are scraped with a sharp flat-edged iron tool.

quotes.quote: While for the harder stones this is done by chiseling out the extra material, with softer stones this is done by scraping out the same with a sharp flat-edged iron tool.

claims.text: The EPCH report on the Bhubaneswar project says finer detailing takes up the majority of the carving time.

quotes.quote: Finer detailing takes up majority of the time of carving.

claims.text: In the GI process, muscular definitions are further improved and finally all surfaces are meticulously finished.

quotes.locator: G.I. Application Number 87, (J) Method of production, Process, p. 61
quotes.quote: Muscular definitions are further improved. Finally, all surfaces are meticulously finished.

claims.text: The EPCH report says sanding smooths the edges and removes file marks, by hand with sand paper or on a smoothening plate.

quotes.quote: Sanding is done on the structure to smooth the edges and to remove all the file marks. This can be carried out manually using a sand paper or same can be imposed on a smoothening plate.

claims.text: The EPCH report says hand polishing applies a traditional polishing powder with a soft, moist muslin cloth, and the final polishing is done with zinc powder.

quotes.quote: Hand polishing of the base article is done using a traditional polishing powder which is applied on the surface with a soft, moist muslin cloth.
The final polishing is done using zinc powder.

claims.text: As filed, the GI application stated that computer-controlled cutters cannot yet improve upon works finished by hand.

quotes.locator: G.I. Application Number 87, (J) Method of production, p. 61
quotes.quote: Computers controlled cutters etc., cannot yet improve upon works finished by hand.

claims.text: The GI application says every block of stone or marble demands a slightly different approach because of its own unique nature.

quotes.locator: G.I. Application Number 87, (J) Method of production, p. 61
quotes.quote: every block of stone or marble demands a slightly different approach to the next piece because of its own unique nature.

claims.text: The GI application lists tools known by Odia names, among them tagi (chisel), gunati (double sided chisel), thuk thuka (wooden hammer), mugura (heavy wooden hammer, spelt heaw in the scanned form) and matama (iron angle).

quotes.quote: known by special local names given in Oriya areTagi (chisel) Gunati(double sided chisel) Thuk thuka (wooden hammer) Mugura (heaw wooden hammer) Matama (iron angle)

claims.text: The GI application also lists ghasa stone (sharpening stone), hand saw, ouha (file), rounder (compass), hand drill, triangular, flat, half round and round files, and tools named tanki, guntha, tuli and muna.

quotes.quote: Tanki Ghasa stone (Sharpening stone) Hand saw Guntha Tuli Muna Ouha (file) Rounder (compass) Hand Drill Triangular file Flat fileHalf round file Round file

lede.text: Konark Stone Carving is a geographical indication of Odisha for stone statues of gods and goddesses, nature and human forms, Konark wheels, candle stands and other goods, produced mainly at Konark in Puri district and at Bhubaneswar.
The GI application says the work is confined to the Pathuria caste, with surnames such as Das, Mistri, Nayak and Maharana, and dates the art back to the late 6th or early 7th century AD.
It names serpentine stone as the craft's most important feature, and Odisha Tourism lists soapstone, chlorite, khondalite and black granite among the stones Odisha's carvers handle.

Konark specialises in icons and figures carved in different dance poses, and the sculptures adorning temples, among them the 13th-century Sun Temple at Konark, provide the models for the carvers' motifs.

sentences.text: The GI journal says the craftspersons of the Kalinga School built masterpieces such as the Sun Temple at Konark, which was built in the 13th century under King Narasimha Deva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty.
UNESCO describes the temple as the culmination of Kalingan temple architecture.
A V&A relief of King Narasimha I with his spiritual advisor, made in the 2nd quarter of the 13th century, belongs to a series that originally decorated the temple's walls.
The GI application says the work is confined to the Pathuria caste, as an Odia inscription of 1604 mentions, and calls Konark a centre of the art's origin.
Odisha Tourism says the progeny of the temple builders have kept their forefathers' sculptural traditions alive, and that a few surviving ancient texts on the art are followed closely.
Paramparik Karigar writes that sculptors of India's stone carving traditions follow the Shilpa Shastras, guidelines on stone measurements and techniques of sculpting.
Sudarshan Sahoo, born in Puri in 1939, established the Sudarshan Crafts Museum in Puri in 1977 and received the Padma Shri in 1988 and the Padma Vibhushan in 2021.
Padma Shri sculptor Pravakara Maharana, a resident of Sujanagar near Gop, began training at the Orissa State Handicraft Training Centre in Bhubaneswar in 1975.
Odisha Tourism says that, whether the stone is hard or soft, an outline is first drawn on stone already cut to size, and the figure is brought out by removing the unwanted portions.
In the GI method of production, the traced design is given a crude shape, then the final carving is carried out and the items are polished.

The block of stone is broken down into main planes, its surface drilled to various depths and a rough body outline made before the intricate work, after which tool marks are removed with flat chisels.
Odisha Tourism says harder stones are chiselled, while softer stones are scraped with a sharp flat-edged iron tool.

Finally all surfaces are meticulously finished; the EPCH report describes sanding with sand paper, hand polishing with a traditional powder on a moist muslin cloth and a final polish with zinc powder.

The GI journal lists serpentine, which looks solid grey at first and turns translucent green when worked, granite from Moyurbanj for heavy work, sandstone (saan patar) for rough big sculpture and soft red naali stone.

Odisha Tourism lists ultra soft white soapstone (khadipathara), greenish chlorite (kochilapathara), pinkish khondalite (sahanapathara or baulapathara) and black granite (mugunipathara), the hardest of all.
Sources differ on khadipathara, which a Millennium Post feature gives as the local name of serpentine, and on the main stone, which the Orissa Reference Annual gives as khondalites and granites.

The EPCH report describes a soft pink stone brought from the Barbil areas that polishes to mottled bright pink, green to black, and says Pathuriasahi craftsmen at Puri carve replicas of temple sculptures in pink stone and hard kochila.
The adhesive car patch fixes and dries within 15 minutes, and Araldite takes 12 to 24 hours to join stone and is used for its strong bonding.
The Konark Sun Temple itself was built of poor-quality khondalite throughout, with chlorite for doorframes and a few sculptures and laterite in its foundation.
The stone is called serpentine because its colour and markings resemble the skin of snakes.
Serpentine comes in multicoloured green, pink, grey and black, with a dull to greasy lustre and a greasy feel, and is soft compared with other dark rocks.
In mineralogy, serpentine may refer to any of 20 minerals of the serpentine group.
None of the stones of the Konark Sun Temple was available near the site, so the material was brought long distances.
The GI journal divides the sculptures of Konark's artists into four categories: the divine, the secular figure, the world of flora and the world of fauna.
The figures generally carved depict Odissi dance poses (mudras) and are dressed and ornamented with traditional Orissan garments and jewellery.
Temple sculptures provide the models for motifs such as alasa kanyas, salabhanjikas, surasundaris, the nava grahas, the Konark wheel and horse, and composite figures such as gajabidala and gajasimha.
Other motifs represent deities such as Krishna and Radha, Laxmi, Vishnu, Durga, Buddha and Ganesh, and recent articles include ash trays, paperweights, candle stands and bookrests.
Odisha's carvers also make images for installation in temples as presiding deities and parswadevatas, and large pieces to decorate public places.
The Orissa Reference Annual names the Sun temple wheel as the most famous of the modern decorative pieces.

UNESCO counts 24 carved wheels on the temple, each about 3 m in diameter, while World History Encyclopedia's introduction gives 12, and UNESCO's descriptions differ on whether six or seven horses draw the chariot.

The Orissa State Cooperative Handicrafts Corporation Limited filed GI application 87 on 9 April 2007 in class 19, though a Millennium Post feature refers to the memorandum filed with the GI registry in 2008.
The application was published in Supplementary Journal 1, dated 24 March 2008, and certificate number 69 is dated 10 July 2008, with registration valid up to 8 April 2027.
The GI registry's list of authorised users runs to serial number 2.
Sources differ on inspection: the GI journal names an inspection body that includes the Managing Director of Utkalika, while the application as filed left inspection to customers and retailers.
In December 2016 the EPCH ran a 25-day stone craft workshop at Bhubaneswar for 40 artisans under National Awardee Susil Kumar Maharana.
A Development Commissioner (Handicrafts) official told the EPCH designer in 2016 that exports dealt with the same product line and were steadily declining.
The GI journal names Konark in Puri district and Bhubaneswar with its outskirts as the main areas of production.
Odisha Tourism says Odisha's stone carving is practised mainly at Puri, Bhubaneswar and Lalitgiri in Cuttack district, with some artisans at Khiching in Mayurbhanj district.
The Konark Sun Temple stands on the shores of the Bay of Bengal, about 35 km northeast of the city of Puri.
